key_insight: Coach-BP detected five blood pressure measurement technique criteria from clinic video with a mean AUROC of 0.93.
clinical_relevance: Automated technique assessment could support more consistent blood pressure measurement, but effects on blood pressure accuracy and patient outcomes were not reported.
method: Analyzed front- and side-camera recordings using pose, visual context, and audio-visual features.
Trained machine learning models on clinician labels for five guideline-recommended technique criteria.
Evaluated against expert ratings using leave-one-participant-out cross-validation and simulated camera artifacts.
evidence_signal: In 408 encounters from 225 participants at one academic center, mean AUROC was 0.93 (95% CI 0.90–0.94) and mean balanced accuracy was 0.88 (0.85–0.90).
watch_item: Single-center cross-validation does not establish performance in other settings or the effectiveness of real-time corrective coaching.
paper_title: Coach-BP: Computer Vision-Based Assessment and Correction of Blood Pressure Measurement Technique
